chapter: Wynn: New York and Chicago bands
title: Luis Russell's band and leaving New York
summary: Without a release from Chicago, he could only gig with Luis Russell, and then left for Chicago.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: They said, no, you're still originally a member of Chicago.

I couldn't start a regular job on the, on the, on the, and yet I hadn't paid any dues. And so it was just one of those things. I mean everybody tried to straighten it because during that time, Bushbaum was in and he knew me. And he tried his best, but he said, no, you got to stay that waiting period out. Well, Louis Russell had a very good band at that time. Hickey was with him and everything. Well, Louis was just gigging around. So I made a few dates with them. And Louis said, well, you can come on in the band as a regular member anytime you like to. But by me not being able to take a regular job, it's sort of just taking all the spirit out. I even, uh, taking one of those dancing schools, I say, well, maybe I can go down there. In those days you could get, they work you, work you like, like the Dickens. But I said, maybe I can hide out down there for a while and keep me going until I get, uh, my status straightened out. But men finally come down there and say, Al, I don't want to cause any trouble. Say, but the next time I catch you, boy, I got to turn in. There's nothing I can do but turn in. So I got disgusted and said, well, I'll come on out to Chicago. So I'll come on out here.
